reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Arachidonic acid" -> "increased membrane fluidity" -> "enhanced cell signaling" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Cholesterol" -> "maintains membrane integrity" -> "prevents excessive fluidity" -> "decreased fluidity" -> 70%

analysis: The fluidity of the plasma membrane is influenced by the types of fatty acids and other molecules present. Arachidonic acid, being an unsaturated fatty acid, has a kinked structure that prevents tight packing of phospholipids, thereby increasing membrane fluidity. In contrast, cholesterol can decrease fluidity at high concentrations by filling spaces between phospholipids, leading to increased rigidity. Both palmitic acid and stearic acid are saturated fatty acids, which promote tight packing and thus decrease fluidity. Given this information, the most supported option for increasing plasma membrane fluidity is indeed arachidonic acid.
